newsitem.title: CROATIA: Widow asks the Hague to retry Croatian cop killer.
newsitem.headline: Widow asks the Hague to retry Croatian cop killer.

text.p: The widow of a murdered Croatian police chief has asked The Hague war crimes tribunal to retry the suspected killer after his 20-year jail sentence was annulled by the Croatian Supreme Court, the state news agency HINA said on Tuesday.

Josip Reihl-Kir, the head of police in the eastern town of Osijek, was murdered in a car in July 1991. Kir favoured dialogue with minority Serbs who had shortly before started their rebellion against Croatia's independence.

The murder took on wide political implications as rumours leaked that Reihl-Kir's statements, had he lived, could have blamed senior Croatian officials for stirring nationalist hostilities at the onset of war in 1991.
He knew his life was in danger and was due to be transferred to Zagreb the day after he died.
Antun Gudelj confessed to having sprayed the caras carrying Reihl-Kir and three other officials with bullets. Three of the four were killed and one badly wounded.
Gudelj, 49, was tried in absentia and sentenced to 20 years in jail in 1994.

He appealed to the Supreme Court, claiming he should be released under a general amnesty which Croatia had issued for Serbs who took part in the 1991-95 rebellion. The Court approved his appeal last week.
In his defence he claimed he had no intention of killing Reihl-Kir but shot at the Serb car because he had heard rumours that Serbs had hanged his father and mined his house.

Reihl-Kir's widow filed a complaint against the ruling to Croatia's Constitutional Court and asked the Hague-based International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY) to retry Gudelj, HINA quoted her lawyer as saying.

Under its statute ICTY has the right to re-open a case if it deems a war-related trial by a national court has not been impartial or the case was not diligently prosecuted. However, the rule applies only to suspects indicted by the tribunal.
